response: Yes, the Hawkins sign is able to predict the absence of necrosis in fractures of the neck of the talus (also known as the astragalus). It is a radiographic sign that appears as a subchondral lucency or a "sclerosis" line in the talus on an X-ray taken 6-8 weeks after the injury. The presence of the Hawkins sign suggests that the blood supply to the talus is intact, reducing the risk of avascular necrosis.
